title: One Question You Need to Ask Every Day
author: Greg McKeown
summary: McKeown challenges the assumption that knowing people well means understanding them. A study in the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology shows spouses are no more accurate than strangers at decoding ambiguous statements. The solution is embarrassingly simple: ask instead of guess. Rather than spending hours trying to get inside someone's head, leaders should ask direct questions about what matters most. This simple shift from assuming to asking transforms communication with customers, teams, and families.
points: Relationship proximity increases confidence without corresponding increases in actual accuracy.
Direct asking outperforms guessing about what others want or need.
Five minutes of conversation can replace hours of wrong assumptions.
Leaders constantly miss this obvious step with customers and teams.
The shift from guessing to asking requires intentional habit change.
quotes: We don't misunderstand because we lack intuition but because we don't ask them.
The relationship actually increased confidence not accuracy at understanding them.
You can spend hours trying to put yourself in someone else's shoes or spend five minutes asking them what it feels like.

Ask your team what the friction points right now and how you can help reduce them. Stop guessing and start asking people what they actually need from you.” Archived from 1-Minute Wednesday Newsletter on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
